info.title: Threefold Governance Sidecar API
info.description: Autonomous coding agent governance sidecar and cost circuit-breaker. Deterministic code decides: it scans arguments for credential shapes, refuses writes that cross a Clean Architecture boundary, halts a session that repeats a cycle of tool calls, and caps projected spend. Amazon Bedrock (Claude Haiku 4.5) only phrases the verdict, and every response says which of the two produced the sentence it carries, in explanation_source. Certificates are SHA-256 fingerprints over a session's verdicts: they detect corruption, not an adversary, because nothing signs them.

servers.description: Live deployment, eu-west-1. Answers an anonymous request with no key.
Local runtime, started by make run.

post.description: Evaluates tools in native OpenAI function_call or Anthropic tool_use JSON formats.

200.description: Normalized evaluation result, with the same verdict fields POST /evaluate-tool-call returns under evaluation

400.description: The body is not a JSON object.

get.description: Returns the sessions the service has evaluated, newest first. This is the contract the sessions console renders. The listing scans the session table, which is honest at this scale only; a deployment with real traffic wants a secondary index on a recency key. The calls field counts retained history, which the store caps at the last fifty per session.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return. Clamped to between 1 and 200.

200.description: Session summaries, with the persistence mode of the most recent write

persistence.description: Where the most recent session write landed. It does not describe where the rows below were read from.

post.description: Evaluates one tool invocation against the credential scanner, the layering rules, the loop detector and the budget. A hook sends this before the tool call runs, and the pages send it too; agent, origin and explain say which of the two a row came from, so a visitor pressing a button on the dashboard is never counted as an agent being governed. The loop gate treats the two differently. For origin hook, a detected loop refuses the repeating call with BLOCKED_LOOP_DETECTED and records it, but never halts the session: session_tripped stays false and the next different call is judged as usual, so a governed developer is not locked out of their own session. A session whose id starts sim-, and a call from a page, keep the terminal halt: the third identical call is refused, the session is frozen and every later call is refused with BLOCKED_CIRCUIT_BREAKER until an operator resumes it. Repeats of read-only or polling calls (git status, log, diff or show, ls, cat, pwd, gh run view, list or watch, sleep, and reads) are recorded as observations and are never refused as a loop.

session_id.description: What the loop detector counts against. A caller that shares one id between users shares a halt with them.

project_name.description: Required. A name that does not match the stack's AllowedProjectPattern (default ^Acme-[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,40}$), or no name at all, is stored, counted and used as the metric dimension as 'unlabelled', and the response says so in warnings.

developer.description: Either 'anonymous' or a 12-character hex hash computed on the caller's machine, never a user name. developer_id is still accepted from older callers. Pages that list decisions show any developer value only as a short hash.

developer_id.description: What this field was called before the v2 request. New callers send developer.

arguments.description: The call's own arguments. For a write these carry the text being written, which is what the layering rules read.

agent.description: Which caller sent the call: claude-code, codex, antigravity, pre-commit, ci or page. Stored on the ledger row. Any other value is recorded as 'unknown' and reported in warnings.

origin.description: hook, page or ci. Stored on the ledger row. Any other value is recorded as 'unknown' and reported in warnings.

explain.description: Whether a refusal gets a sentence from Amazon Bedrock. Default true, which is what the pages send. Hooks send false, and the verdict then carries the deterministic reason with explanation_source 'deterministic' and no model call. An approved call is never sent to the model.

dry_run.description: Default false. When true the call is evaluated and recorded as observed: it is never refused and never trips the session, and the rule that would have refused it is returned under observations. A repository installed in observe mode sends every call with dry_run true.

hook_mode.description: The mode the hook on the developer's machine runs in: observe sends every call as a dry run, managed leaves the decision to the project's stage on the server, enforce never sends a dry run. Stored on the ledger row. Absent, or any other value, is recorded as 'unknown'; another value is reported in warnings.

200.description: Evaluation verdict, the invariants it was measured against, and the explanation with its source

status.description: APPROVED, or the name of what refused it.

rule_evaluations.description: Each invariant and whether this call satisfied it.

session_tripped.description: Whether the session is now halted, so that every later call is refused until an operator resumes it. A loop refused for origin hook leaves it false; a loop in a sim- or page session sets it.

explanation_source.description: What produced bedrock_explanation: bedrock when the model answered, deterministic_fallback when it did not.

observations.description: What a rule in observe mode would have refused. The call still ran.

warnings.description: What the service changed or ignored on the way in, for example a project name stored as 'unlabelled'. Always present, empty when nothing was changed.

project_stage.description: The calling project's stage on this stack: its own when configured, otherwise the stack's DEFAULT_HOOK_STAGE (default observe). The stage decides only calls with origin hook or ci that are not dry runs: observe judges them exactly as a dry run is judged, recorded and never refused; enforce runs the gates, except that a refusal under one of the project's observe_rules is recorded as an observation. Page and scenario calls always enforce. Reported on every verdict, whether or not it applied.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object, or a number in it cannot be used: a negative token count, or a budget of zero or less.

post.description: Issues a SHA-256 fingerprinted Governance Certificate over a session's verdicts. The fingerprint is unkeyed: it detects corruption and casual edits, not an adversary, because nothing signs it and nothing in CI requires one before a merge.

200.description: The certificate, returned rather than archived

400.description: The body is not a JSON object, or there is nothing to certify: an empty list of evaluations, or a session this service has no record of governing

get.description: Retrieves runtime governance thresholds (max spend, loop thresholds, blocked patterns).

200.description: Current policy configuration

post.description: Adjusts the runtime governance thresholds. This write is durable: it lands in DynamoDB and every container that starts afterwards adopts it, so it requires the operator key even on a deployment where reads are anonymous. The handler rebuilds the whole policy from the body, so send all four fields; blocked_patterns is not accepted and is discarded.

200.description: Updated policy configuration

401.description: No key was presented, and this deployment requires one for policy writes

403.description: The key was rejected, or this deployment has configured no policy-write key at all

get.description: Verifies downstream dependencies (DynamoDB, Bedrock, S3, Webhook Dispatcher). HEAD answers with the same status and no body, so an uptime check need not download the breakdown on every probe.

200.description: Subsystems health breakdown

get.description: Retrieves cumulative spend, history length and circuit breaker status for a session that has been recorded. Reading never creates a session.

200.description: Current session statistics

404.description: No session with this id has been recorded (urn:threefold:error:session-not-found)

post.description: Immediately freezes and terminates an autonomous agent session, revoking further tool executions.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays the first response for a repeated key instead of freezing twice. Allowed through CORS, so a page served from another origin may send it.

200.description: Session frozen confirmation

post.description: Lifts the halt on a recorded session, so its next call is evaluated again instead of refused with BLOCKED_CIRCUIT_BREAKER. Requires the operator key even where reads are anonymous, because it undoes a halt the gate or an operator made. The body names who cleared the halt and why, and both are kept on the session as the record of it. History and spend are kept too, so a session past its budget, or repeating the call that halted it, halts again. Never creates a session.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays the first response for a repeated key instead of resuming twice.

requestBody.description: The record of who cleared the halt and why. Both are required, because that record is the reason this route needs the operator key; a value over its length is refused rather than cut, since a shortened record says something its author did not.

example.reason: Budget raised for the Acme-Billing migration; resuming the same session.

200.description: The session is no longer halted

previous_trip_reason.description: The halt this resume cleared, as the session recorded it; empty when it recorded none.

400.description: operator_name or reason is missing, is not text, or is longer than its limit (urn:threefold:error:bad-request, naming the field); nothing was changed

403.description: The key was rejected, or this deployment has configured no operator key at all

404.description: No session with this id has been recorded (urn:threefold:error:session-not-found), so there is nothing to resume and nothing is created

409.description: The session is running, not halted (urn:threefold:error:session-not-halted), so there is nothing to clear and nothing was changed

post.description: Simulates 3 consecutive identical file edits in a sim- session to demonstrate circuit-breaker tripping. The demo keeps the terminal halt: call 3 is refused and the session is frozen. A hook's loop refuses the repeating call without halting the session; see /evaluate-tool-call.

200.description: Loop interception verdict with Bedrock explanation

post.description: Simulates an agent attempting to export AWS access keys, tripping the Secret Scanner.

200.description: Security block verdict

get.description: The hook itself: one standard-library script that puts Threefold in front of Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity, served as readable text rather than as a download a reader cannot inspect, and answered without a key even where reads are private, because a product nobody can obtain is a demo. The agent is detected from the shape of its input, or named with --agent. The same file is served at /hooks/claude_code_hook.py and /claude_code_hook.py, so an install copied earlier keeps working.

200.description: The script, as text/plain

get.description: Returns health status, active governance rules, and model configuration. HEAD answers with the same status and no body, for a monitor that wants the code and not the body.

200.description: Operational status and active rules

get.summary: What the gates decided, by project, kind of problem and rule
get.description: Aggregates the decision ledger over a window for the Enforcement Console. A refusal and an observation are counted apart: an observation is a call that ran and that a rule in observe mode would have refused. Rows keep the target of a call and never its arguments.

200.description: totals (decisions, refused, approved, refusal_rate, observed, projects, developers), by_category, by_rule, by_observed_rule, by_project, by_developer, by_day, recent_refusals, recent_observations, coverage

get.description: Open, because a reader has to be able to see the architecture they are held to. With project, answers that project's own rules when it has saved some. When it has not, is_default is true and the rules shown are the shared default its calls are judged against until it saves its own. Without project, answers the shared set, as before.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The project whose rules to read, an Acme-style alias such as Acme-Billing.

200.description: rules, count, is_default, languages_read, extensions_read, refresh_seconds, unsupported

is_default.description: Asked with project: true when that project has saved no rules of its own and the rules shown are the shared default, false when they are its own. Asked without: true when the shared set is still the one Threefold ships with.

refresh_seconds.description: How long a server may go on using the rules it holds before reading them again.

post.summary: Replace the layering rules of one project, or the shared set
post.description: Replaces a whole set and stores it. With project, the set is that project's own, stored under CONFIG#rules#<project>, and the gate applies it to calls whose project_name is that project; every other project keeps the shared set. Without project, the shared set is replaced, as before. The save is all or nothing: if any rule cannot be used, nothing is saved and the 400 names each rule and why. The server that takes the save applies the rules from its next call; every other server reads them again within refresh_seconds. Requires the operator key even where reads are anonymous, because the rules are the gate rather than a setting on it.

project.description: The project these rules are for, an Acme-style alias such as Acme-Billing. Leave it out to replace the shared set every project without rules of its own uses.

200.description: RULES_UPDATED, with the rules as stored and refresh_seconds

400.description: At least one rule cannot be used; nothing was saved (urn:threefold:error:unusable-rule)

index.description: Position of the rule in what was sent.

403.description: The key was rejected, or this deployment has configured no operator key at all

post.summary: Try the rules on a file without saving or recording anything
post.description: Reads the imports in the content and judges them against the layering rules in force, or against a draft sent in the body. With project, the rules in force are the ones the gate would apply to that project: its own when it has saved some, the shared set otherwise. Only the layering rules are tried: a write this answers ALLOW for can still be refused for a credential, a protected path, a loop or its cost. No verdict is issued, no ledger row is written and a draft is never put in force, which is why it is open.

path.description: At most 400 characters, on one line, with no spaces: the same test the gate applies before it judges a path.

project.description: Try the rules that project's calls are judged against. A draft sent in rules is tried instead, whatever project says.

rules.description: A draft to try instead of the rules in force.

200.description: language, imports, rules_considered (draft | in force), applicable_rules, verdict (REFUSE | OBSERVE | ALLOW), violations, note, scope

400.description: The body is not a JSON object, has no path, has a path the gate would never judge (urn:threefold:error:nothing-to-explain), or carries a draft with a rule that cannot be used (urn:threefold:error:unusable-rule, with problems)

get.summary: Tiles, a daily series and totals by agent, origin, rule and project, from the rollups
get.description: Read from one rollup item per project and day, added to as every decision is recorded, so the numbers are exact however busy the ledger is. approved, observed and refused are disjoint: observed is a call that ran and that a rule would have refused, and a day's calls are the sum of the three. needs_review is the observed calls nobody has labelled; false_alarms the calls labelled false alarm.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The window, 1 to 30 days ending today.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Only this project.

200.description: window_days, generated_at, source (always rollups), totals, series, by_agent, by_origin, by_rule, by_project, stages

get.summary: The ledger's rows, newest first, filtered and a page at a time
get.description: Reads the ledger day by day from today backwards. Each request reads a bounded number of ledger pages, so a filter that matches little may return fewer than limit rows with a next_cursor: follow it until it is null. The cursor is opaque and resumes exactly after the last row returned.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The window, 1 to 30 days ending today.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Only this project.

parameters.name: rule
parameters.description: Only rows with this rule_key.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: refused, observed (ran, and a rule would have refused it), approved (nothing flagged it), or all.

parameters.name: review
parameters.description: Only rows with this review, or with none.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: Only this agent.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Only this session.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many rows.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor of the previous page.

200.description: items and next_cursor

400.description: A kind, review or cursor this service does not know.

get.summary: One decision, with its session and the layering rule it was keyed by

200.description: decision, session (or null) and rule (the layering rule's definition, or null for a gate)

get.summary: Every configured project, and every project seen in the last 7 days
get.description: Counts are over the last 7 days, from the rollups. A sandbox is listed until it expires.

200.description: projects

configured.description: False for a project seen in the rollups with no configuration; its stage is then the stack default.

get.summary: One project: its configuration and whether each of its rules is ready to enforce
get.description: A project's rules are its layering rules in force plus the gates LOOP, PROTECTED_PATH, UNREADABLE_WRITE and BUDGET. Read from the rollups over the window.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The project, an Acme-style alias such as Acme-Billing.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The window, 1 to 30 days ending today.

200.description: project, config (null when never configured) and readiness

would_refuse.description: Calls it flagged that ran, in the window.

state.description: noisy if any false alarm, else needs_review if any unreviewed, else ready if it flagged anything, else quiet.

404.description: The name is neither an alias this stack admits nor 'unlabelled'.

post.summary: Create or change a project's configuration

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The project, an Acme-style alias such as Acme-Billing.

200.description: The project and its stored configuration.

400.description: The name does not match AllowedProjectPattern, a stage is neither observe nor enforce, or a rule key is not one of the project's rules (its layering rules in force plus LOOP, PROTECTED_PATH, UNREADABLE_WRITE and BUDGET).

post.summary: Enforce the rules picked; every other rule of the project keeps observing
post.description: Sets stage enforce and observe_rules to the project's rules minus enforce, and adds a history entry.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The project, an Acme-style alias such as Acme-Billing.

200.description: The project and its stored configuration.

400.description: The name does not match AllowedProjectPattern, a stage is neither observe nor enforce, or a rule key is not one of the project's rules (its layering rules in force plus LOOP, PROTECTED_PATH, UNREADABLE_WRITE and BUDGET).

post.summary: Back to observe, in one step
post.description: Sets stage observe and adds a history entry. observe_rules is kept, so a promotion undone is one step to redo.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The project, an Acme-style alias such as Acme-Billing.

200.description: The project and its stored configuration.

400.description: The name does not match AllowedProjectPattern, a stage is neither observe nor enforce, or a rule key is not one of the project's rules (its layering rules in force plus LOOP, PROTECTED_PATH, UNREADABLE_WRITE and BUDGET).

post.summary: Label what a rule flagged: correct, false alarm, or clear
post.description: The label is stored on the ledger row itself, conditionally on the row belonging to this project, with reviewed_at, review_note and reviewed_by, which is 8 hex of a hash of the credential presented (X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer), never the credential, or anonymous. A row of another project, a row nothing flagged, or an item that cannot be read is skipped with its reason.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The project, an Acme-style alias such as Acme-Billing.

200.description: updated and skipped

reason.description: other-project, not-found, nothing-flagged, or why the item could not be read.

400.description: items is not a list of 1 to 100 reviews, or the name does not match AllowedProjectPattern.

post.summary: A throwaway project, seeded, for trying the review and promotion walk
post.description: Creates Acme-Sandbox-<8 hex> in observe with sandbox true and a 24 hour expiry, and sends a dozen synthetic hook calls from claude-code, codex and antigravity through the real evaluator. Several would be refused under more than one rule, and one of them is a false alarm: a test module under tests/domain/ that the domain rule's path pattern also covers.

200.description: project, calls_seeded and the dashboard url

409.description: This stack's AllowedProjectPattern does not admit sandbox names.

OperatorApiKey.name: X-API-Key
OperatorApiKey.description: Operator key for writes that outlive the request. Reading needs none. A deployment that has configured no key refuses policy writes outright with 403.

id.description: What a refusal quotes. Must be unique within the set.

description.description: The sentence a developer reads when stopped.

mode.description: enforce refuses the write. observe lets it run and records that the rule would have refused it. A missing or null mode means enforce. Any other value makes the whole save fail with 400, naming the rule.

when_path_matches.description: A list of globs over the file path, at most 40, each at most 300 characters. ** crosses folders, * and ? stay inside one. Case is ignored.

forbid_imports.description: A list of at most 40 patterns. A dotted or slashed module prefix forbids it and everything beneath it, never a sibling that only shares its first letters. Globs are allowed.

allow_imports.description: Exceptions, a list of at most 40. When an allow and a forbid both match, the more specific pattern decides.

DecisionRow.description: One ledger row, as a public page may show it: the project is an Acme-style alias or 'unlabelled' and the developer an 8-hex hash. Never the call's arguments or file content.

developer_id.description: An 8-hex hash, never the value sent.

rule.description: The invariant that failed, or NONE. Kept as it always was.

rule_key.description: What decided the call, and what readiness, reviews and observe_rules group by: the id of the layering rule that decided, or LOOP, PROTECTED_PATH (which also covers destructive commands), UNREADABLE_WRITE, CREDENTIAL, BUDGET, HALTED_SESSION, or NONE when nothing flagged the call. Set on observations as well as refusals. Rows written before it existed are given one on the way out.

stage.description: The stage the call was judged under. A dry run is observe, a page call is enforce.

hook_mode.description: observe, managed, enforce or unknown, as the hook sent it.

ProjectConfig.description: A project's stage configuration, stored at PK=CONFIG#project#<name>.

observe_rules.description: Rule keys whose refusals are recorded as observations while the project enforces.

sandbox.description: True for a sandbox, which is gone 24 hours after it was made.

by.description: 8 hex of a hash of the credential used, or anonymous.
